findings.claim: The patch skips the only postgres integration test of storage-server startup and /metrics instead of fixing it. This removes coverage for a supported backend and hides the startup failure that eager Init exposes.

verifier.reason: The patch adds a `t.Skip` for `dbType == "postgres"` with a `TODO - fix this test for postgres` at pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35-38, and this is the only test that targets `modules.StorageServer` and checks `/metrics` (line 45 is the sole test reference), so with sqlite already skipped only mysql still runs it. The same patch adds eager `s.Init(ctx)` in `NewResourceServer` (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258-262); that this is what breaks postgres in Drone is plausible but not provable from source alone.

findings.claim: The test hardcodes db_host 'localhost' for postgres, but Drone runs postgres at host 'postgres'. Startup therefore fails when eager init opens the DB in NewResourceServer.

verifier.reason: The test still hardcodes `db_host` "localhost" for postgres (pkg/server/module_server_test.go:76) while Drone sets `POSTGRES_HOST: postgres` (scripts/drone/steps/lib.star:1071), and the patch's eager `s.Init(ctx)` (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258) now opens the DB at startup via the backend lifecycle hook (pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go:94-106). The patch masks this rather than fixing it by skipping the test for postgres (module_server_test.go:36-38), so CI does not actually fail; the failure itself was traced statically, not run.

findings.claim: The function-wide cacheMu lock was removed from BuildIndex, so concurrent callers (e.g. a Search request and handleEvent via getOrCreateIndex) can build the same key at once. The last writer wins, one built index goes untracked or its documents are lost, and file-backed indexes can be created concurrently in the same directory.

verifier.reason: The patch drops the function-wide lock in BuildIndex and only guards the final `b.cache[key] = idx` (pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:88-139), while getOrCreateIndex still does an unsynchronised GetIndex-then-build (pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:292-298), so Search (search.go:148) and handleEvent (search.go:237) can build the same key at once and the last write replaces the other index. The file-backed part is narrower: getOrCreateIndex passes size 10 and the default threshold is 10 (pkg/setting/setting_unified_storage.go:44), so same-directory `bleve.New` at bleve.go:98 only races when the threshold is configured below 10.

findings.claim: File-based indexes above index_file_threshold are created with bleve.New(dir) under a deterministic path. bleve v2 returns ErrorIndexPathExists when that directory already exists and nothing removes or reopens it, so NewResourceServer fails on every restart after the first.

verifier.reason: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:97-98 calls bleve.New on the deterministic path Root/namespace/resource.group, and nothing under pkg/storage removes or reopens it (no RemoveAll or bleve.Open), so on restart the error propagates through search.go:190-197 and the Init call the patch added at resource/server.go:258-262. bleve v2.4.3 is not vendored here, so ErrorIndexPathExists rests on bleve's documented contract for New (path must not exist), not on source I read; the bleve.New call predates the patch, which only moved the failure from first request to NewResourceServer.

findings.claim: Eager Init runs inside the wire graph for every Grafana process on context.Background() with no deadline. A DB or search failure or hang now blocks Grafana startup.

verifier.reason: The patch adds an eager `s.Init(ctx)` to `NewResourceServer` (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258-262) on a `context.Background()`-derived context with cancel but no deadline (server.go:229). That constructor is reached from the wire provider `ProvideUnifiedStorageClient` (pkg/storage/unified/client.go:67,101; pkg/server/wire.go:212), so a DB migration/ping or search-index build error or hang (server.go:296-311) now fails or stalls startup instead of the first request. "Every process" is slightly overstated: the `unified-grpc` storage type builds only a client (client.go:78-97) and search init is feature-flagged.

findings.claim: With the per-request s.Init(ctx) check removed, handlers (Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search, History, Origin, PutBlob, GetBlob) no longer reject requests after Stop is called. Writes can then reach the still-open DB with the poller cancelled, so Watch returns io.EOF and no events are published.

verifier.reason: The patch removes every per-request `s.Init(ctx)` guard, which was the only reader of the `initErr` that `Stop` sets (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:321,339), so handlers no longer reject requests after `Stop`. `Stop` only cancels `s.ctx` and the backend poller without closing the DB (server.go:333, pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go:119-121, 577), so writes still go through while `Watch` gets `io.EOF` from the terminated broadcaster (pkg/storage/unified/resource/broadcaster.go:131-132, 206).

findings.claim: IsHealthy reports healthy while the server is stopping or stopped.

verifier.reason: `Stop` records "service is stopping"/"service is stopped" in `s.initErr` (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:321,339), but the patch removed the `s.Init(ctx)` guard that surfaced it, so `IsHealthy` now only delegates to `s.diagnostics.IsHealthy` (server.go:934-935). That delegate returns SERVING unconditionally for the default noop (noop.go:27-31) or whenever the DB ping succeeds for the SQL backend (pkg/storage/unified/sql/backend.go:109-117), whose `Stop` only cancels a context.

findings.claim: With the per-request Init calls removed, initErr has no reader after construction, so the writes to initErr in Stop are dead code.

verifier.reason: The only remaining caller of `server.Init` is `NewResourceServer` (pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258) and `Init` is not on the `ResourceServer` interface (server.go:27-32), so the "stopping"/"stopped" writes at server.go:321 and :339 are never read and no longer reject requests after `Stop`. One caveat: the write at server.go:328 is still read locally by `return s.initErr` at server.go:337.

findings.claim: The sync.Once and initErr gating in Init are dead scaffolding. Init's only caller is the constructor, *server is unexported, and Init is not on the ResourceServer interface, so the once guard can never be hit twice.

verifier.reason: After the patch the only call to `(*server).Init` is in the constructor at pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258; every per-RPC `s.Init(ctx)` call was removed, `ResourceServer` (server.go:27-32) has no `Init`, and no code type-asserts to an interface with `Init`. So `s.once.Do` (server.go:294) runs exactly once per instance, and `initErr` is only a local accumulator there — the values `Stop` writes to it (server.go:321-339) are never read by any request path.

findings.claim: There is an untracked TODO about the RV short-circuit optimization.

verifier.reason: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:100 has a bare comment `// TODO, check last RV so we can see if the numbers have changed` with no issue link or owner; the patch converted it from a `b.log.Info("TODO, ...")` call into this comment, leaving the RV-check optimisation unimplemented and untracked.

findings.claim: Docstring coverage is 0.00%, below the required 80.00% threshold.

verifier.reason: The patch touches only Go files and adds no new functions or types, and the repo has no docstring-coverage gate or 80% threshold (.golangci.yml:8-11 configures revive with no such rule; no interrogate-style config exists). The 0.00% figure is also wrong on its face, since touched code carries doc comments, e.g. pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:171 and pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:923.

findings.claim: The init error is logged twice with the identical message 'error initializing resource server', once inside Init and once in NewResourceServer, and is also returned to the caller.

verifier.reason: `Init` logs `"error initializing resource server"` at pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:314 and returns the error at :317; the patch-added call in `NewResourceServer` logs the identical message at :260 and returns the same error at :261, so one init failure produces two identical error log lines plus a returned error.

findings.claim: When Init fails, NewResourceServer returns (nil, err) without calling cancel() or lifecycle.Stop. This leaks the context, and if search.init succeeded before initWatcher failed, it also leaks the search watch goroutine and its sql poller.

verifier.reason: pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258-262 returns (nil, err) on Init failure without s.cancel() or s.lifecycle.Stop, and the caller gets nil so it cannot call Stop either. With Init now ordered search.init then initWatcher (server.go:303-311), a failing initWatcher leaves the search watch goroutine (search.go:202-213, on context.Background()) and the sql poller (sql/backend.go:566-578, which exits only on b.done, closed by backend.Stop) running.

findings.claim: No test covers NewResourceServer returning lifecycle/search/watcher init errors or handlers working without lazy Init. apistore/watcher_test.go still calls Init manually before construction, which is now redundant.

verifier.reason: Mostly correct: the new eager-init error return at pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258-262 has no failing-path test, since every test caller asserts require.NoError (server_test.go:52, apistore/watcher_test.go:125,156, sql/test/integration_test.go:59), and watcher_test.go:148 still calls the backend's Init before construction, which is redundant but harmless (sync.Once at sql/backend.go:86-91). The "handlers working without lazy Init" part is wrong: server_test.go:88-109 calls List/Create/Read straight after construction.

findings.claim: In searchSupport.init with initWorkers > 1, totalBatchesIndexed++ is a non-atomic increment from multiple concurrent goroutines, which is a data race.

verifier.reason: pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:189 does a plain `totalBatchesIndexed++` on a captured local int inside `group.Go` closures, and the errgroup limit is `s.initWorkers` (search.go:179), so with more than one worker the increments run concurrently with no mutex or atomic. The value is only read for a trace span attribute at search.go:199, and the patch did not touch these lines.

findings.claim: In searchSupport.init with initWorkers > 1, errgroup goroutines write the shared outer err variable without synchronization (assigned with = rather than :=), so one worker's error can be overwritten by another's nil and lost. The narrowed lock makes these builds truly parallel.

verifier.reason: In pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:190-191 each errgroup goroutine does `_, _, err = s.build(...)` then `return err` on the outer `err` declared at line 181, with no synchronization, so a concurrent worker's nil can overwrite another's error before it is returned and `group.Wait()` (line 195) never sees it. The patch does narrow `cacheMu` in pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:137-139 so builds run in parallel, but the racy assignment is in lines the patch did not change and was already outside that lock.

findings.claim: bleveBackend.TotalDocs iterates b.cache without holding cacheMu, while BuildIndex writes the map concurrently. Callers include the new startup log in searchSupport.init (after the watch goroutine starts) and BleveIndexMetrics.Collect on every scrape, so concurrent map iteration and write can cause a fatal runtime panic.

verifier.reason: pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:144-154 ranges over b.cache with no cacheMu lock while BuildIndex writes the map at bleve.go:137-139; TotalDocs is called from the new log at resource/search.go:216 (after the watch goroutine starts at search.go:207, which can reach BuildIndex via handleEvent) and from the registered collector at resource/bleve_index_metrics.go:96, so an unsynchronised map read/write is possible. The unlocked TotalDocs and the Collect caller predate the patch; the patch adds the search.go:216 call site.
